This is a real, demonstrable speech-frame marker at the 52:7|52:8 seam — the row's own rationale quotes the closing quotation mark itself. The identical device (a fronted, contrastive first-person pronoun opening a new movement) is treated as the decisive tier-1 driver for a strophe break elsewhere in this same review set, at the seam 55:15|55:16 (web:Ps.55.16 = “As for me, I will call on God. The row's rejected_alternative asserts ‘no further speech-frame marker separates’ 52:6-7 from 52:8-9; that claim is contradicted by the row's own quoted evidence and by the standard applied to the parallel construction elsewhere in the set.

reviews.reasoning: Re-derived rather than trusted. WEB quotes verbatim-confirmed; dual-cite arithmetic for this shift+1 psalm (title = MT v1) is correct throughout (web:Ps.53.0 = oshb:Ps.53.1 etc.), matching citation_sweep.py GREEN. The Elohim/YHWH count is independently reproduced two ways — sweep.py --skel over oshb:Ps.53.2-Ps.53.7 gives 7 total אלהים tokens across 5 of 6 verses (Ps.53.2,53.3,53.5,53.6,53.7) and 0 יהוה tokens, and psalm_device_inventory.json's yhwh_elohim_per_psalm entry for psalm 53 independently records {yhwh:0, elohim:7} — both matching the row's claim exactly (sweep: 7 occurrences, 5 verses). However, the row's closing sentence misidentifies two Hebrew words. Splicing oshb:Ps.53.7 directly from source: “מִ֥י יִתֵּ֣ן מִצִּיּוֹן֮ יְשֻׁע֪וֹת יִשְׂרָ֫אֵ֥ל בְּשׁ֣וּב אֱ֭לֹהִים שְׁב֣וּת עַמּ֑וֹ יָגֵ֥ל יַ֝עֲקֹ֗ב יִשְׂמַ֥ח יִשְׂרָאֵֽל”. The row cites יִתֵּ֣ן and glosses it ‘Zion’, and cites יְשֻ֥עוֹת and glosses it ‘Israel’. Neither gloss is correct: יִתֵּ֣ן is the verb ‘he/it will give’ (root נתן), and יְשֻ֥עוֹת is ‘salvations of’ (construct plural, root ישע). The verse's actual words for Zion and Israel are the third and fifth words — מִצִּיּוֹן֮ (‘from Zion’) and יִשְׂרֶ֫אֵ֥ל (‘Israel’). This is a quote/gloss mismatch on the row's own cited original-language evidence, not a byte-fidelity problem (all four words collate at byte tier against their verse).

challenges.claim: The row mislabels two Hebrew words at oshb:Ps.53.7 as meaning 'Zion' and 'Israel'; neither gloss is correct.
challenges.evidence: Full verse spliced from source, web:Ps.53.6 = oshb:Ps.53.7: “מִ֥י יִתֵּ֣ן מִצִּיּוֹן֮ יְשֻׁע֪וֹת יִשְׂרָ֫אֵ֥ל בְּשׁ֣וּב אֱ֭לֹהִים שְׁב֣וּת עַמּ֑וֹ יָגֵ֥ל יַ֝עֲקֹ֗ב יִשְׂמַ֥ח יִשְׂרָאֵֽל” (collate.py tier: byte). Word-by-word: word 2 יִתֵּ֣ן = ‘he/it will give’ (root נתן), NOT ‘Zion’ as the row states; word 4 יְשֻ֥עוֹת = ‘salvations of’ (construct plural, root ישע), NOT ‘Israel’ as the row states. The words that actually carry those referents sit at word 3, מִצִּיּוֹן֮ (‘from Zion’, containing the root ציון), and word 5, יִשְׂרֶ֫אֵ֥ל (‘Israel’) — both present in the same verse but not the tokens the row cites. The WEB rendering the row quotes, web:Ps.53.6 = “Oh that the salvation of Israel would come out of Zion! When God brings back his people from captivity, then Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.”, correctly reflects the verse's sense (salvation coming out of Zion for Israel); only the row's word-level Hebrew attribution is backwards.

Re-derived the strophe's closing seam independently. web:Ps.55.19 = “God, who is enthroned forever, will hear and answer them. Selah. They never change and don’t fear God.”, and its MT counterpart oshb:Ps.55.20 splices to “יִשְׁמַ֤ע אֵ֨ל וְֽיַעֲנֵם֮ וְיֹ֤שֵׁ֥ב קֶ֗דֶם סֶ֥לָה אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֵ֣ין חֲלִיפ֣וֹת לָ֑מוֹ וְלֹ֖א יָרְא֣וּ אֱלֹהִֽים” (collate.py: byte tier). Selah sits mid-verse, not at its end: the clause “אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֵ֣ין חֲלִיפ֣וֹת לָ֑מוֹ וְלֹ֖א יָרְא֣וּ אֱלֹהִֽים” (= 'They never change and don't fear God') follows it in the same verse, and that clause is itself the content the row calls 'a verdict on the unrepentant'. The rationale states the strophe is 'closed by the psalm's second Selah at web:Ps.55.19' — but the Selah does not close the verdict; the clause after it does. Policy caps Selah at tier-3-like corroboration, never a driver or closer, and the row's own observed_substrate_signals separately (and more accurately) calls it 'corroborating (not driving)' — the rationale's phrasing is the part that overstates Selah's structural role, and it is the sort of selah-adjacent-close overreach the review brief specifically asks reviewers to test.
